abstract_research_topics.justification: This domain focuses on theories and techniques for generating code using machine learning, which is an abstract research topic due to its emphasis on the underlying methods and innovations.
Code language models (LLMs) are a theoretical area as they involve developing models to understand and process code, focusing on model architecture and capabilities rather than specific applications.
This domain involves researching how models interpret and process programming code, which is highly abstract and theoretical.
This topic encompasses both the theoretical understanding of code semantics and the generation of code, focusing on the abstract algorithms and methods involved.
While initially seeming practical, this domain involves gathering and analyzing empirical data to validate theoretical models and assumptions about software engineering processes.
Though applied, this domain leans toward theoretical exploration of search algorithms and their optimization in software testing contexts.

application_domains.justification: Focused on practical methods to generate test inputs that can be used in real-world testing scenarios.
This domain applies testing methodologies specifically to autonomous systems, a practical application in ensuring their reliability and safety.
A practical field focusing on methodologies to test and ensure software quality, directly applicable to real-world scenarios.
Concerned with the application of software testing to video games, this domain is clearly a practical application of testing principles.
Focuses on testing methodologies for machine learning models, applying practical techniques to ensure model integrity and performance.
Involves applying techniques to detect errors at runtime in software applications, making it a direct application domain.
Identifying potential runtime errors in applications before they occur is an applied field focusing on real-world applications of predictive techniques.
An applied research area that involves techniques to analyze and fix bugs in software systems, directly impacting software development.
While it involves some theory, program analysis is applied to understanding and improving software execution, making it a practical field.
Typically involves creating code from higher-level specifications, focused on the applied aspect of generating executable programs.
A practical application focusing on creating summaries of code for easier maintenance and understanding by developers.
Deals with practices and methodologies in the development and maintenance of open source projects, a practical field with real-world applications.
Application of educational methodologies to teach programming, a field focused on real-world application in academic and skill-building contexts.
Although this could involve abstract research, in this context, it is a practical application related to language design and use.
Focuses on applying methods to automatically fix bugs in software, a direct application of theoretical methods to improve software reliability.
Involves real-world practices to maintain and evolve existing software systems, a clear application domain.
Concerned with ensuring software reliability, a practical domain applying engineering principles to software systems.
Uses analysis techniques on software data for insights, directly applied in practical contexts to improve software development processes.
A broad area focused on the application of engineering principles to software development, a clear application domain.
